provider: iiif.archive.org (free IIIF Image API over any uploaded image)

free_tier.stated: No separate quota — it is a free image server over items you already hold, one image per item. Capacity therefore follows the 1TB/item rule.

retention.stated: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.

egress.terms: Free, and it is a rendering endpoint, so one stored master serves arbitrary region/size/rotation/quality requests — the cheapest possible way to serve image bytes at many sizes

tooling: IIIF Image API v2 and v3 (Cantaloupe server); any IIIF viewer or plain GET on /iiif/<identifier>/info.json; no rclone backend
limits_note: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Third-party workshop doc, not IA's own page
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: (snapshot 2026-07-12) — 'The Internet Archive allows you to upload images and then provides a IIIF Image API service ... images can be accessed as either Version 2 or Version 3'
same page — 'Ensure you only upload 1 image (if you want multiple images you will need to create multiple items ... collection is Community Image'
